description: Enlarge an image 2× or 4× with on-device AI super-resolution (the same models as ruah.tools/upscale — the image never leaves this computer). Unlike `resize`, it redraws detail and crisp edges instead of stretching pixels into blur. Made for small or low-resolution images: icons, thumbnails, old web images, small product shots. Saves a new file and returns its path plus a small preview; the original is never changed. The result is limited to 16.8 megapixels (4096×4096): ×4 fits inputs up to about 1000×1000, ×2 up to about 2000×2000. To make an already large photo bigger, use `resize` with allow_upscale. Time grows with the output: small images take seconds, ×4 of 1000×1000 a minute or more. Transparency is kept: a transparent logo, icon or cut-out comes back transparent, with no dark fringe (save as png, webp or avif to keep it). The first ×2 call downloads an 8 MB model once, the first ×4 call 55 MB.

format.description: Output format: keep = same as the input; webp = usually smallest, keeps transparency; avif = smaller still, slower; jpeg = photos only, transparency becomes white; png = keeps transparency. Default keep.

input_path.description: Image file to upscale (jpg, png, webp, avif, gif, tiff; heic on macOS). Absolute, ~/…, or relative to the working directory.

lossless.description: png only: keep exact colours. Default true; false makes a smaller palette PNG.

output_path.description: Where to save. Default: "<name>-upscaled-x2.<ext>" (or -x4) next to the input. Existing files are never overwritten.

quality.description: 1–100 for webp/avif/jpeg. Default 90, like the web upscaler.

scale.description: 2 = twice the width and height (default — quicker, and enough for most images); 4 = four times, for genuinely tiny sources.

name: upscale
title: Upscale image (AI)
